summary: The candidate made four rounds of blind edit-test cycles on src/sweep.ts without ever stating a hypothesis or narrating their reasoning, and even after an interviewer nudge pointed directly at the partial-shipment semantics, the final edit still failed the test. The session ended with tests still failing and no fix landed or root cause articulated.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate never read the failing test body or asked any clarifying question about what partially shipped holds should return on expiry. They went straight to editing sweep.ts without articulating what behavior was expected, and even after three failed attempts did not ask about the semantics until the interviewer's nudge forced the question.

There is no narrated hypothesis at any point — the candidate opened sweep.ts and immediately started editing without naming a mechanism, and repeated this blind edit-test cycle three times with the same failure. Even the location (sweep.ts) was correct, but no mechanism like 'releasing original count vs remaining' was ever stated before the nudge.

Across nearly seven minutes and four edit-test cycles, there is no recorded narration of what the candidate was reading, suspecting, or trying — only silent edit/save/test actions. An interviewer would have had no way to follow their reasoning without interrupting, which is exactly what happened.

The candidate made three separate edits to the same file that each failed the same test, indicating undirected trial-and-error rather than a coherent fix strategy, and even the fourth edit made after the explicit nudge still failed to fix the test.

They did consistently re-run the test suite after every edit rather than declaring success blindly, which is the right instinct, but this diligence never led to a passing state and the session ended on a failing run with no further investigation.

The session ended with the candidate clicking End Session immediately after another failed test run, with no articulation of root cause, no explanation connecting any edit to the failure mechanism, and the bug was never fixed.
